jobs.title: Rådgjevar innan digital informasjonsforvaltning og utvikling
jobs.description:
Som rådgjevar innan digital informasjonsforvaltning og utvikling vil du få

vere med å utvikle korleis NTNU forvaltar, deler og nyttar informasjon på ein framtidsretta og berekraftig måte.

I denne stillinga får du arbeide i skjeringspunktet der teknologi møter fag og menneske. Du vil støtte tilsette i arbeidskvardagen, gjere komplekse tema forståelege og bidra til smartare og meir brukarvennlege arbeidsprosessar.

NTNU moderniserar no saksbehandlings- og arkivområdet, mellom anna gjennom overgangen frå Elements til WebSak. Du får høve til å ta del i denne utviklinga og bidra med opplæring, rådgiving, systemstøtte og forbetring av digitale løysingar.

Ved NTNU får du ein variert arbeidskvardag, ei brei kontaktflate og høve til å påverke utviklinga av fagområdet. Du blir ein del av eit sterkt fagmiljø som deler kunnskap, utforskar nye løysingar og samarbeider på tvers av campusane ved NTNU.

Arbeidsplassen din er ved campus Ålesund, med tett samarbeid med kollega ved NTNUs øvrige campus. Du får ei sentral rolle i utviklinga av framtidas informasjonsforvaltning ved NTNU, samt varierte arbeidsoppgåver innan digitalisering, automatisering, KI og nye systemløysingar. Du vil også få ta del i eit sterkt, tverrfagleg fagmiljø med gode moglegheiter for utvikling og påverknad i lag med 32 andre medarbeidarar.

Du vert tilsett i seksjon for informasjonsforvaltning. Seksjonssjefen er din næraste leiar.

Kva vil arbeidskvardagen din bestå av?

Opplæring og kompetanseutvikling

Planlegge og gjennomføre opplæring og utvikle digitale læringsressurser for saksbehandlere.

Rådgivning og veiledning

Gi råd om informasjonsforvaltning, dokumentasjon, saksbehandling og relevant regelverk.

Systemstøtte og brukerstøtte

Bistå brukere og utføre systemadministrative oppgaver i aktuelle saksbehandlingsløsninger.

Utvikling av systemer og arbeidsprosesser

Bidra til innføring av WebSak og forbedring av rutiner, systemer og integrasjoner.

Digitalisering, automatisering og KI

Utforske og ta i bruk teknologi som kan effektivisere og forbedre NTNUs tjenester.

Kvalitet og kontinuerlig forbedring

Utføre arkivfaglige oppgaver og bidra til kvalitet, etterlevelse og videreutvikling av fagområdet.

For å vere kvalifisert for stillinga, må du ha

relevant høgare utdanning på minimum bachelornivå. Omfattande relevant erfaring kan kompensere for utdanningskravet
relevant erfaring frå informasjons- og dokumentasjonsforvaltning, arkiv eller saksbehandling
erfaring med sak- og arkivsystem eller andre relevante informasjonsforvaltningsverktøy
erfaring frå offentleg forvaltning og kjennskap til relevant lov- og regelverk
god digital kompetanse og samarbeidsevne
god munnleg og skriftleg framstillingsevne på norsk og engelsk

Det er ein fordel om du også har kompetanse innan:

digitalisering, automatisering eller bruk av kunstig intelligens
opplæring, kompetanseutvikling og formidling
systemadministrasjon, testing, brukarstøtte, databasar eller integrasjonar
arkivfagleg arbeid og utvikling av effektive arbeidsprosessar
universitets- og høgskulesektoren eller anna offentleg verksemd

Vi forventar ikkje at du kan alt. Det viktigaste er at du er nysgjerrig på nye løysingar og motivert for å utvikle deg saman med oss.

For å trivast og lykkast godt i stillinga, ser vi for oss at du er

nysgjerrig, utviklingsorientert og ser moglegheiter for forbetring. Du tek initiativ, arbeider sjølvstendig og systematisk og finn gode løysingar på utfordringar. jobs.title: Machine Learning Engineer III, Routing Cost
jobs.description:
Mapbox is the leading real-time location platform for a new generation of location-aware businesses. Mapbox is the only platform that equips organizations with the full set of tools to power the navigation of people, packages, and vehicles everywhere. More than 4 million registered developers have chosen Mapbox because of the platform’s flexibility, security and privacy compliance. Organizations use Mapbox applications, data, SDKs and APIs to create customized and immersive experiences that delight their customers.

What We Do

The Navigation team at Mapbox develops and operates web services powering virtually all of Mapbox’s strategic navigation initiatives in consumer, automotive, and logistics verticals. We are a highly multidisciplinary organization, with work spanning distributed systems on AWS to geospatial localization, traffic telemetry, and mapping.

Collectively we are revolutionizing in-car experiences with technology to build fast, industry-leading maps and navigation for any vehicle. We’ve launched products such as MapGPT, Mapbox for EV, and we’re enhancing the visual experience of in-vehicle navigation with 3D styling with our new Mapbox Standard through web and mobile SDKs. Mapbox has worked with automotive partners — including BMW, Toyota, and GM — to bring the best aspects of mobile app development into in-vehicle navigation and infotainment.

Mapbox Blog: Introducing 3D Live Navigation
Mapbox Blog: Route Notifications Improve Driver Safety
Mapbox Newsroom: AI Features in New Navigation SDK

As AI becomes embedded in modern engineering workflows, we value engineers who can thoughtfully integrate AI into design, development, and decision-making. Our interview process will include discussion of how you use AI in your engineering workflow.

What You’ll Do

As a Machine Learning Engineer III on the Routing Cost team, you will lead the design, development, and delivery of highly trafficked recommendation systems for our routing cost engine. Your technical contributions will include:

Lead the engineering team(s) to execute end-to-end feature implementation within the larger navigation organization (~80 engineers).
Design and build new ML and data pipelines, as well as optimizing existing ML and data pipelines.
Build tools for automated quality assurance and data exploration.
Leverage geospatial algorithms to optimize pipelines, as well as creating automated tuning and outlier detection algorithms.
Partner with data scientists to make improvements to our models for determining patterns in movement and/or traffic.
Mentor colleagues and participate in code and design reviews.
Participate in an on-call rotation to ensure our systems remain available to customers 24/7. Team members alternate as the on-call primary responder, which may require immediate response outside normal working hours, including weekends.

What We Believe Are Important Traits For This Role

8-10+ years of backend and ML experience: Extensive hands-on experience showcasing expertise and a strong track record in the engineering field.
Technical knowledge: Extensive experience with Python, distributed processing pipelines (Hadoop, Spark, Airflow, Dask), and very large datasets – statistical analysis, data quality control, optimizing storage.
Cloud proficiency: Extensive experience with cloud and infrastructure services, including, as well as deploying and managing infrastructure in cloud environments.
Operational excellence: You drive a culture of quality and continuous improvement in your organization. Strong passion for clean code and robust architecture, with a drive to elevate engineering practices and design standards across the team.
Ownership & execution: Own the technical vision, lead the strategy and guide the team to execute towards building the future of our routing cost engine.
Customer focus: You care deeply about your customers and their problems, and you work tirelessly to innovate on their behalf.
Growth mindset: Have the humility to accept mistakes, learn and grow from them.
Mentorship: Experience mentoring and leading engineering teams developing skill sets and career growth.
Strong written and vocal communication skills: You can talk and write about complex ideas concisely to a wide audience. You are able to lead and resolve org-wide technical discussions and are able to collaborate and include input from cross-functional teams (security, devops, data, compliance and product).
Data informed mindset: You believe in the value of data informed decision making and strive to measure things that are not straight forward but essential. You also have the right instincts to make speedy decisions in the absence of perfect & comprehensive data

What We Value

In addition to our core values, which are not unique to this position and are necessary for Mapbox leaders:

We value high-performing creative individuals who dig into problems and opportunities.
We believe in individuals being their whole selves at work. We commit to this through supportive health care, parental leave, flexibility for the things that come up in life, and innovating on how we think about supporting our people.
We emphasize an environment of teaching and learning to equip employees with the tools needed to be successful in their function and the company.
We strongly believe in the value of growing a diverse team and encourage people of all backgrounds, genders, ethnicities, abilities, and sexual orientations to apply.

By applying for this position, you acknowledge that you have received the Mapbox Non-US Privacy Notice for applicants, which is linked here. Completing this application requires you to provide personal data, such as your name and contact information, which is mandatory for Mapbox to process your application.

We are committed to a fair and equitable hiring process. We do not discriminate against any protected class.

jobs.title: Data Engineer
jobs.description:
Would you like to build data solutions that make a real difference in how Veho operates and makes decisions?

At Veho, we have strengthened our data capabilities and developed a modern data environment based on Microsoft technologies. As we continue to develop our data platform and make better use of data across our business, we are looking for a Data Engineer
to join our Group-level Data & Analytics team.

In this role, you will work across the data and analytics stack, from building data pipelines and developing our data platform to creating data models and reporting solutions. You will play an important part in making data reliable, accessible, and valuable for our business.

What will you do?

As a Data Engineer, you will join our data platform team within the Data & Analytics function, reporting to the Head of Data. You will work closely with other Data Engineers, our Data Platform Engineer, business analysts, and stakeholders across the organization.

Your focus will be on building and improving the technical solutions that enable data to flow smoothly from different source systems into reporting and analytics. You will be involved in both new development and the continuous improvement of existing solutions, with responsibility for delivering reliable and practical results.

Your key responsibilities will include:

Building and maintaining ETL processes and data pipelines that integrate data from different source systems.
Developing and improving our data platform, including data warehousing and data processing solutions.
Designing, developing, and maintaining Power BI semantic models and reports.
Supporting the reliability, quality, and continuous improvement of our data platform and analytics solutions.
Independently delivering smaller development initiatives while contributing to the team's wider projects and goals.

You will have the opportunity to apply your technical expertise to real business challenges, develop practical solutions, and see the impact of your work across the organization.

What are we looking for?

We are looking for a hands-on Data Engineer who enjoys working with modern data technologies and solving practical challenges. You have a solid technical foundation and experience in developing data solutions, but most importantly, you are motivated to learn, take responsibility, and contribute to a collaborative team.

We hope you bring:

Excellent SQL skills and good practical knowledge of Python.
Hands-on experience in building and maintaining modern data warehouses, lakehouses, or data platforms.
Experience with Microsoft cloud data technologies, particularly Azure Synapse and/or Microsoft Fabric.
Practical Power BI skills, including working with semantic models, DAX, and report development.
A good understanding of data modelling and data integration principles.
Familiarity with software development practices such as version control, testing, and CI/CD.
Good communication and teamwork skills, with the ability to collaborate with both technical colleagues and business stakeholders.

Experience with Microsoft Power Apps
is considered an advantage.

We value a structured, analytical, and proactive approach to work. You enjoy hands-on problem-solving, can work independently within your area of responsibility, and are eager to develop your skills. Openness, honesty, and a collaborative mindset are equally important to us.

As we work in an international environment, fluency in English is required.
Finnish language skills are considered an advantage.

Why Veho?

Meaningful work with business impact.
You will help ensure that reliable data is available for reporting, analytics, and business decision-making across our international operations.
A modern data environment and experienced colleagues.
You will join a Data & Analytics organization of approximately ten professionals, working with Microsoft technologies including Azure, Power BI, and Microsoft Fabric.
A diverse international environment.
Our operations across five countries and several business areas offer opportunities to work with different data sources, systems, and business needs.
Opportunities to develop your expertise.
You will have the opportunity to take ownership of your work, develop your technical skills, and contribute to the continuous improvement of our data platform.

Your workplace will be at Veho's office in Aviapolis, Vantaa. We follow a hybrid working model that includes three days per week at the office. Free parking is available onsite.

If you would like to develop data solutions that support business reporting and decision-making at Veho, we would be happy to hear from you.

jobs.title: Finance AI & Digital Facilitator
jobs.description:
About the role

As a Finance AI & Digital Facilitator, you will help build an AI- and digital-first Finance function. You will partner with Business Controlling, Financial Controlling, Tax, Treasury and Financial Transactional Services to identify opportunities that reduce manual and transactional work and enable greater focus on business partnering, insights and decision support.
You will facilitate the definition of target states and turn identified opportunities into deliverable solutions. From the outset, the role combines transformation facilitation with agile project management and end-to-end delivery ownership. Initially, the focus will be on establishing the transformation pipeline; over time, the role will become more evenly balanced between facilitation and solution delivery.

Key responsibilities

Partner with Finance teams to identify opportunities where AI and digital solutions can fundamentally transform work, create value and increase capacity for higher-value activities.
Design and facilitate senior-level workshops that help each finance subfunction define ambitious objectives and agree on clear, business-owned target states.
Document signed-off target states, including scope, metrics, timelines and resourcing, while maintaining consistent and auditable templates and progress tracking.
Gather requirements and baseline data, conduct value and benefit analyses, and maintain business cases that demonstrate efficiency gains and changes in how Finance delivers value.
Manage multiple initiatives using agile practices, including backlog management, iteration planning, dependency and risk tracking, and delivery reporting.
Own opportunities from initial shaping through delivery, adoption and value tracking, connecting finance stakeholders with engineering teams and providing clear progress updates.

What we are looking for

Strong workshop design and facilitation skills, with experience engaging senior stakeholders, challenging established thinking and building alignment around transformational objectives.
Good understanding of finance processes—such as closing, controlling, tax, treasury or transactional services—and how digitalisation can shift work toward business partnering, analysis and decision support.
Experience in business analysis, target-state design, requirements definition, value modelling and stakeholder negotiation, together with good BI literacy.
Hands-on agile project and delivery management experience, including managing backlogs, iterations, risks and dependencies across several parallel workstreams and supporting solutions through adoption.
A Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in business, finance, industrial engineering and management, or a related field, with relevant experience in business analysis, process consulting, agile delivery or organisational change.

Service design training and agile certifications are considered advantages.

Growth opportunities

The role will initially focus on facilitation and building the transformation pipeline across Finance. As more opportunities progress into development, the balance will shift toward agile delivery and solution ownership. Over time, the role can develop into broader programme or delivery management responsibility as the Finance transformation portfolio grows.

tukemaan yrityksemme kasvua, vahvistamaan brändiemme näkyvyyttä ja vauhdittamaan myyntiä tuloksellisella digitaalisella markkinoinnilla.

Pääset hyödyntämään vahvaa digitaalisen markkinoinnin osaamistasi ja viemään ideasi käytäntöön. Suunnittelet ja optimoit digitaalista markkinointia, jolla vaikutat suoraan liiketoimintamme tuloksiin.

Miksi meille?

Tässä roolissa pääset aidosti vaikuttamaan digitaalisen markkinointimme kehittämiseen ja sitä kautta liiketoimintamme kasvuun. Veeva is the industry cloud for Life Sciences. We are enabling agentic biopharma through applications, agents, data, and consulting working together. Learn more about our products, vision, values, and status as a Public Benefit Corporation (PBC) on our website.

Consulting is changing, and Veeva Business Consulting is not like other firms. Launched in 2019, we’ve grown quickly and organically to over 500 global experts who combine deep industry knowledge and unique insights to accelerate drug development and commercialization for our customers.

We are growing aggressively and seeking great people to help Life Sciences work in a more efficient and connected way, shaping the future of the industry with the world’s leading AI applications, agents, and data at their back.

The Role

We are hiring recent university graduates to grow the next generation of consultants through our Business Consultant Development Program (BCDP).

We believe in pushing high potential people to achieve excellence. Our program is specifically designed to provide a challenging environment to learn quickly and deliver value early. You will collaborate with experienced team members on customer-facing engagements to create high-impact business solutions.

In our structured 18 month program, we equip you with the resources to develop the core consulting skills, deep domain expertise, and leadership foundation for long-term career success at Veeva.

BCDP spans five core practice areas: Analytics, Commercial, Content, R&D, and Quality. As an Associate Consultant you will align to one of those practices, allowing you to build targeted industry expertise. You will be asked to choose your preferred practice in the application process.

You can learn more about our practices and the work we do here.

The anticipated start date is September 2027.

What You'll Do

Support and deliver all components of customer engagements (e.g., customer communications, workshops, stakeholder interviews, process and data analysis, managing timelines)
Collaborate with Business Consultants to create deliverables that optimize customer operating and engagement models, processes, and business performance
Leverage Veeva’s applications, agents, and data to pull through tangible business and operational solutions

REQUIREMENTS | We are looking for graduates who meet the following requirements:

2027 university graduate with strong academic performance
Desire to work within an intense, challenging program and environment
A process-driven person who loves digging into operations, numbers, and other data to find opportunities for improvement
Excellent verbal and written communication skills
Fluent in written and spoken English
High work ethic. Veeva is a hard-working company
High integrity and honesty. Veeva is a PBC and a “do the right thing” company, and we expect that from all employees
Willingness to travel up to 20% of your time per year. Travel varies per customer engagement, coworking, internal meetings, and events with your team
Explore More Generation Veeva Roles: We welcome you to apply to all roles that align with your skills and interests. See all open opportunities here: Generation Veeva Careers

THE PROCESS | Our process is different than most. It is designed to be fast, efficient and respectful. Here are the steps:

Application: You submit your resume, short cover letter of questions, and take a personality test (unless you have already completed it with Veeva previously). Within one week we will notify you via email if we would like to move you to the next stage
Leader Interview: The next step is an interview with a leader of the practice
Case Exercise: If we proceed, you will be invited to complete a case exercise within a week
Offer: Within one week after completing your case exercise, we will extend you an offer or let you know that we do not wish to move forward. You will have two weeks to make your final decision. If you accept, we will hold a spot for you and expect you to show up on your start date. Accepting an offer and continuing to interview would be an ethical violation in our view

Compensation

Starting Salary: 38,000 EUR
After one year, if you perform well, you will receive a significant salary increase and be granted equity

Work Authorization:
Qualified candidates should be legally authorized to be employed in the EU.

Work Environment:
Veeva is a Work Anywhere company. You can choose to work in an office or remotely from home on any given day of the week - it’s up to you! Although Veeva is Work from Anywhere, Associate Business Consultants must live within a maximum commuting distance of 45 minutes to 1 hour from Veeva’s Barcelona office.

jobs.title: Robotics Mechanical Design Engineer
jobs.description:
Who We Are

Helsing is a defence AI company. Our mission is to protect our democracies. We aim to achieve technological leadership, so that open societies can continue to make sovereign decisions and control their ethical standards.

As democracies, we believe we have a special responsibility to be thoughtful about the development and deployment of powerful technologies like AI. We take this responsibility seriously.

We are an ambitious and committed team of engineers, AI specialists and customer-facing programme managers. We are looking for mission-driven people to join our European teams – and apply their skills to solve the most complex and impactful problems. We embrace an open and transparent culture that welcomes healthy debates on the use of technology in defence, its benefits, and its ethical implications.

The role

As a Robotics Mechancial Engineer, you will play a key role in the design and development of our robots. You will be responsible for creating robust and efficient mechanical mechanisms, assemblies, and systems that integrate with advanced robotic technologies. This is an exciting opportunity to work with a multidisciplinary team of engineers, bringing together expertise in mechanical, electrical, and software engineering.

The day-to-day

Design and develop mechanisms, systems, and electromechanical assemblies for robotic applications, including structures, actuators, and motion systems.
Collaborate closely with the electrical and software engineering teams to ensure seamless integration of mechanical designs into complete robotic systems.
Prototype, test, and iterate on mechanical designs to meet performance, cost, and manufacturability requirements.
Analyze project specifications, materials, and manufacturing methods to ensure that designs meet both functional and production objectives.
Use CAD tools (SolidWorks) to create detailed designs, 3D models, and engineering drawings.
Participate in design reviews, contributing innovative solutions and improvements.
Conduct simulations, stress analysis, and FEA to ensure reliability, durability, and safety of the designs.
Provide technical support and troubleshooting during product development and manufacturing processes.
Stay up-to-date with the latest developments in robotics and mechanical design to incorporate cutting-edge technologies into our products.

You should apply if you

Hold a bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering or related field (Master’s preferred).
Have demonstrated of experience in mechanical design, preferably in robotics or automation.
Are proficiency with CAD software (ideally SolidWorks).
Have a strong understanding of mechanical principles, including statics, dynamics, and material properties.
Have experience with FEA, simulations, and mechanical stress analysis tools.
Have hands-on experience with prototyping and testing.
Are familiar with manufacturing processes such as CNC machining, 3D printing, sheet metal manufacturing and injection molding.
Have excellent problem-solving skills, with the ability to work independently and within a team.
Have strong communication and collaboration skills to work with cross-functional teams.
Have experience with robotics, automation, or mechatronics systems is highly desirable.

Join Helsing and work with world-leading experts in their fields

Helsing’s work is important. You’ll be directly contributing to the protection of democratic countries while balancing both ethical and geopolitical concerns
The work is unique. We operate in a domain that has highly unusual technical requirements and constraints, and where robustness, safety, and ethical considerations are vital. You will face unique Engineering and AI challenges that make a meaningful impact in the world
Our work frequently takes us right up to the state of the art in technical innovation, be it reinforcement learning, distributed systems, generative AI, or deployment infrastructure. The defence industry is entering the most exciting phase of the technological development curve. Advances in our field of world are not incremental: Helsing is part of, and often leading, historic leaps forward
In our domain, success is a matter of order-of-magnitude improvements and novel capabilities. This means we take bets, aim high, and focus on big opportunities. Despite being a relatively young company, Helsing has already been selected for multiple significant government contracts
We actively encourage healthy, proactive, and diverse debate internally about what we do and how we choose to do it. Teams and individual engineers are trusted (and encouraged) to practise responsible autonomy and critical thinking, and to focus on outcomes, not conformity. At Helsing you will have a say in how we (and you!) work, the opportunity to engage on what does and doesn’t work, and to take ownership of aspects of our culture that you care deeply about

What we offer

Competitive salary and VSOP options
Relocation support: up to €2,500 and 4 weeks temporary accommodation
Learning: €500/£450 yearly allowance
Health & wellness: gym membership and mental health support (Nilo.health)
Social: regular company events and monthly social allowances
Enhanced parental leave: 22 weeks fully paid for primary caregivers & 6 weeks for secondary caregivers
Family support: 5 days of paid family emergency leave, 100% remote work option during pregnancy and phased return to work
A hands-on onboarding program (affectionately labelled “Infraduction”), in which you will be building tooling and applications to be used across the company. This is your opportunity to learn our tech stack, explore the company, and learn how we get things done - all whilst working with other engineering teams from day one (Specifically for engineering and AI)

These are the core benefits across all locations, there may be additional benefits in certain locations.

Helsing is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability or gender identity. Manufacturing Science & Technology (MSAT) serves as the global enabling function for the Sensors & Cartridges (S&C) network. Our daily collaboration is grounded in four core values: Courage, Transparency, Open-Mindedness, and a Can-Do Attitude.
Based at our site in Rotkreuz, this role sits within the Product & Process Science (PPS) group. You will apply hands-on precision dispensing expertise directly where it matters most: on the production floor, working shoulder-to-shoulder with process engineers, shift operators, and quality teams to stabilize processes, minimize scrap, and boost product quality.

The Perfect Candidate: has expertise in (electro-chemical) sensors, sensor manufacturing or (electro-, analytical-, technical) chemistry. He/She is knowledgeable about processes in the chemical labs, manufacturing and quality control. The candidate is familiar with leading continuous improvement projects and used data science (programming, statistics etc.) in previous roles or projects to support data-driven decisions. The role includes communication, collaboration and alignment with interfaces ranging from the engineering team to shopfloor, which the candidate brings with him.

General Information:

Start Date: to be discussed
Planned Duration of Employment: unlimited contract via Hays
Workplace: Rotkreuz
Workload: 100%
Home Office: most unlikely

Tasks & Responsibilities

Conduct on-the-ground investigations across the manufacturing line to identify root causes of WIP yield loss, downtime, and dispensing-related deviations; design and execute concrete remediation plans.
Spend consistent, hands-on time on the production floor observing multi-shift runs, partnering closely with operators and shift leads, and upskilling staff from an engineering perspective.
Fine-tune, characterize, and troubleshoot multi-platform automated dispensing equipment, with an emphasis on low-viscosity fluid behavior, surface interaction, and tight tolerances.
Plan, run, and evaluate production-line trials, applying structured problem-solving (e.g., DOE, root-cause methodology) to stabilize fluid deposition and process repeatability.
Analyze sensor production and quality control data to track variability, spot drifting parameters early, and prove the statistical effectiveness of corrective actions.

Deep Precision Dispensing Expertise (Min. 5+ Years). A track record of turning troubleshooting into verifiable production improvements (e.g., scrap reduction, cycle-time stabilization, yield improvements) backed by data
You thrive at the machine side, enjoy working directly with operators across shifts, and communicate comfortably in an active manufacturing environment
A completed technical degree (BSc/MSc in Process, Mechanical, Chemical, Materials, or Biomedical Engineering) or a completed vocational/technical qualification backed by robust, relevant engineering-level experience. Proven technical competence and practical problem-solving capability take precedence over formal titles
Confident using root-cause analysis, basic statistical methods, and structured experimentation to make evidence-based decisions.
Solid understanding of material properties, dispensing parameters and equipment condition
Languages: Fluent English (working project language) combined with German skills at a minimum B2 level to communicate smoothly with shop-floor teams.

Experience within Life Sciences, Medical Devices, Diagnostics, or another highly regulated GxP/GMP manufacturing setting.
Familiarity with sensor manufacturing (e.g., electrochemical/analytical sensors, microassembly, functional coating, or cartridge assembly).
Experience conducting non-conformity/deviation investigations, CAPAs, and technical change-control documentation.
Hands-on familiarity with data tools for statistical process monitoring and data-driven troubleshooting.
Prior background working for or closely interfacing with precision dispensing equipment vendors or automated system integrators.

This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Finance Automation Solution Designer, Global based in Switzerland.

We are seeking an experienced Finance Automation Solution Designer to lead the design of a global finance transformation programme built around Redwood Finance Automation. The role focuses on automating key Record-to-Report processes, including period-end close, account reconciliation, journal processing, and financial reporting. You will take ownership of the solution design, working closely with finance stakeholders to assess existing processes and define the future-state operating model. You will translate business requirements into practical, scalable designs that engineering teams can implement and test. From initial workshops through build, testing, and go-live, you will ensure the solution meets operational, control, and audit requirements. This is a remote contract opportunity for a specialist with proven Redwood implementation experience.

Accountabilities

Responsibilities

You will own the end-to-end solution design and guide its implementation, ensuring that finance automation delivers measurable improvements while maintaining robust financial controls. Your responsibilities will include:

Lead current-state assessments of Record-to-Report processes in collaboration with controllers and finance operations stakeholders.
Design the target automation solution across period-end close, account reconciliation, journal processing, and intercompany activities.
Document the solution design and define how standard Redwood capabilities should be used, identifying where custom extensions are justified.
Design integrations between Redwood Finance Automation, SAP S/4HANA or ECC, and other relevant source systems.
Define balance sheet auto-certification rules, approval workflows, internal controls, and audit trails to support compliant and auditable financial processes.
Guide engineering teams throughout development and review delivered solutions against the agreed design.
Develop the test strategy and acceptance criteria in collaboration with finance users.
Support testing and go-live activities, resolving design challenges as they arise.
Define a roadmap for subsequent phases of finance automation following the initial implementation.

Requirements

The ideal candidate combines substantial finance transformation expertise with hands-on solution design experience in Redwood Finance Automation. You should be comfortable engaging with senior stakeholders and translating complex finance processes into actionable technical designs. Key qualifications include:

Proven ownership of solution design for at least one live Redwood Finance Automation (RunMyFinance) implementation, including leading design workshops and personally producing the solution documentation.
At least 8 years of experience in finance transformation, finance systems, or Record-to-Report process design.
Working knowledge of SAP FI/CO or an equivalent Oracle finance environment.
Understanding of how financial close and reconciliation data flows between ERP systems and finance automation platforms.
Experience facilitating workshops with finance stakeholders and translating business requirements into solutions that can be built and tested.
Strong stakeholder management skills, including the ability to engage senior finance leaders and confidently defend solution design decisions.
Professional fluency in English.

Additional Experience That Would Be Advantageous

Hands-on Redwood configuration or development experience.
Familiarity with BlackLine, Trintech, or SAP Advanced Financial Closing.
A relevant finance qualification, such as ACA, ACCA, or CIMA.
Experience in financial services or another regulated industry, particularly with SOX or comparable audit and control frameworks.

Benefits

Competitive daily rate of GBP 450 for consultants based in the United Kingdom.
Daily rate of EUR 450 for consultants based in Ireland, Germany, the Netherlands, Poland, Romania, Bulgaria, Spain, Portugal, Italy, and Czechia.
Fully remote working arrangement.
Contract opportunity with an expected start date of 15 November 2026.
Opportunity to lead a significant finance automation programme and shape its solution design from initial assessment through go-live.

new_jobs.description:
About VAT Group

At VAT, we change the world with vacuum solutions. As the world’s leading supplier of high-performance vacuum valves, we have been driving innovation for more than 60 years. With over 3,200 employees worldwide, we operate from our headquarters in Haag, Switzerland, with manufacturing sites in Switzerland, Malaysia and Romania, as well as sales and service hubs around the world. We guided by our passions integrity, teamwork, customer centricity, and innovation – always working together as #oneVAT.

Joining us means becoming part of a passionate, international team where your voice is heard, your ideas matter, and your career growth is supported.

Your Challenge

The manufacturing of a high-end microchip requires over 1000 production steps. Vacuum valves are considered to be critical components as they are in proximity to the semiconductor wafer and impact the process performance. Semiconductor fabs like Intel, Samsung or TSMC have increasing expectations for productivity and production yield. These fabs are increasingly using data generated along the manufacturing process to improve production performance. Smart, connected vacuum components are required for smart semiconductor manufacturing fabs enabling predictive maintenance, increasing performance and productivity.

Our products are key components in any semiconductor processing tool worldwide. To extend our market leadership in advanced pressure control for sub-2 nm chip production we want to strengthen our team with experienced engineers with a passion for automation and control systems.

Your responsibilities:

Concept definition and implementation of automation systems for R&D test rigs and laboratory systems
Develop data acquisition and experiment automation functions to test gas sensing and control technology
Development of advanced control algorithms for high performance gas control systems
Develop, perform and document experiments (DoE) including results in organized and structured way
Cooperate among cross-functional teams of experts within VAT R&D organization and external technology partners
Occasional on-site support of newly developed applications/products at customer site.

Your profile:

Engineering Degree (MSc or PhD) in mechanical or electrical engineering, control engineering, mechatronics or similar
Strong skills and knowledge in control system theory and industrial automation
3+ years of industry experience in design and implementation of (semi or fully) automated testing setups
Experience with PLC programming, e.g. Beckhoff, Siemens or similar automation software
Experience with industrial communication protocols
Programming skills in Matlab Simulink or Python
Work experience in vacuum technology / semiconductors beneficial
System engineering knowledge is beneficial
Hands on, systematic approach, creative thinker with problem solving skills and team spirit

new_jobs.title: Data Scientist
new_jobs.description:
Data Scientist

London
4 days/week office
Up to £80,000 + bonus

The opportunity

Our client is a fast-growing intelligence business that helps senior Operations and Supply Chain leaders cut through the noise and make better decisions. They combine proprietary data, member research and AI-native analysis to answer the questions that keep C-suite executives up at night.

Right now they’re riding two of the biggest tailwinds in the market — AI and supply chain — which is a big part of why they’ve grown so quickly since raising funding last year. They’re still only around 100 people and firmly in scale-up mode, so roles here are broad rather than tightly boxed in, with real scope to shape what the position becomes. They want people who bring their own ideas about how things should work, not just execute a brief.

Alongside their Data & Insights function, they’re hiring a Data Scientist to help uncover what’s actually moving the needle on AI and digital adoption in supply chains, and turn that into intelligence their members can act on.

What you’ll actually do

A representative project: proving that specific AI, robotics, or technology implementations are actually having a positive commercial impact — for example, sourcing data points from 10-K filings on whether and how a company mentions a given AI, robotics, or technology implementation, combining that with financial performance data, and then running proper correlation and statistical work to find the patterns that are genuinely commercially relevant, not structuring data for its own sake, but using it to answer a real question about what’s driving outcomes.

It’s a fast-paced environment: you’ll typically have several different projects on the go each month rather than sinking weeks into a single piece of work, so it suits someone who likes variety and moving at pace. You’ll work closely with the Analyst and Research side of the team — they’ll sometimes bring you in on the final client-facing narrative, but the analytical thinking behind it, what the data is and isn’t telling you and why it matters, is yours.
What makes someone good at this

This isn’t a software engineering role — there’s a separate (currently paused) AI Engineer seat for that. It’s a data science and insight role: genuinely comfortable with ambiguity and messy data, and more interested in the “why” behind a correlation than in producing one and moving on.

The people who do well here use AI thoughtfully throughout their process — not just to speed up code, but to explore data, test approaches and sanity-check their own conclusions — while knowing exactly where to stop trusting the output and check it themselves.

Most come from a data science background with a genuinely commercial mindset: someone who has always cared more about the decision an analysis supports than the elegance of the model behind it. Self-starters do particularly well here — if you’ve ever looked at a question and gone and built the dataset yourself rather than waiting for a clean one to land in your lap, this role will make sense to you.

What you’ll need

Around 6-8 years in data science, applied statistics, or a closely related quantitative field — or a shorter track record if you’ve spent time building or running something of your own and are looking to bring that energy into a team
Strong Python and SQL, with real experience building and maintaining data pipelines and transformations, not just running ad hoc queries
Hands-on experience extracting structured data from messy or unstructured sources — documents, filings, scraped or third-party data — and getting it into an analysable state
Genuine statistical and quantitative method: correlation and relationship analysis, feature engineering, transformation logic — data science, not BI reporting
Comfortable in modern data environments (Databricks or equivalent)
Hands-on, critical fluency with AI-assisted development and analysis tools — using them to write code, explore data, and sanity-check findings, while always applying your own judgement on what to trust
Comfort with ambiguity: able to take a loosely scoped question, form your own hypothesis about what’s going on, and iterate toward a defensible answer without needing perfectly defined requirements from the outset
Supply chain or operations domain exposure is a genuine plus, not required

The package

Up to £80,000 plus a bonus scheme, private healthcare and life insurance, enhanced pension, enhanced parental leave and unlimited holiday. Based from a well appointed central London office four days a week, in a small, high trust team that moves fast, expects a lot, and gives a lot of room to grow into shaping what gets investigated next rather than just answering the brief as given.

new_jobs.title: Machine Learning Engineer, Applied AI
new_jobs.description:
Our Mission

Rebuild how the world works, to make institutions work better for the people they serve.

About Brain Co.

Brain Co. builds AI-native operating systems for large, regulated institutions. Each system is built for a specific industry, powered by agents that push real workflows forward. Underneath it all is Atlas, our proprietary platform that keeps customers in control, secure by design, and never locked into one model.

Why Now

Brain Co. is entering its next phase of production deployments on a national scale with an elite team built from Palantir, Google, Meta, and Nvidia, and a growing footprint across government, insurance, health, and financial services.

Joining now means shaping both the company and a new category of applied AI. Every project here ships to production and is expected to create measurable customer value and impact.

You'll work alongside exceptional peers on some of the hardest problems in applied AI. It’s the kind of work you'll still be proud of in ten years from now.

Machine Learning Engineer, Applied AI

About The Role

So much of the work society depends on is still slower and harder than it should be. Permits take months. Claims sit unresolved. And AI hasn't changed that — because the bottleneck isn't the models. It's the institutional context AI needs to do the work: rules, history, relationships, and judgment scattered across people, documents, and legacy systems.

BrainCo exists to fix that. We build agent-native operating systems for the institutions society depends on, and our products are the first of their kind in the world — we were the first, anywhere, to fully automate construction permitting, and we're now doing the same across insurance and other industries. There is no playbook here, because no one has built this before.

As a Machine Learning Engineer on Applied AI, your work begins where the demo ends: getting a model to look impressive is the easy part; making it a production decision system an institution stakes its process on is the job. The problems come in every shape — custom vision model pipelines that check blueprints against building codes at 95%+ accuracy, agents that untangle policy stacks to reveal coverage gaps, systems that predict from clinical records whether a patient is on their care path — and you'll own them end-to-end, from ambiguous customer problem to the eval that catches a whole class of errors.

This is frontier ML applied where it's hardest and matters most. The problems are underspecified, the documents are brutal, the accuracy bar is institutional-grade — and the feedback loops are real, because our systems move real workflows forward every day.

Who We're Looking For

You understand how machine learning actually works — not just the tooling, but the philosophy underneath: what a loss function really optimizes, how generalization breaks under distribution shift, why evaluation is where systems quietly go wrong. And you live at the bleeding edge of modern AI, with hard-won instincts for squeezing the most out of LLMs and agentic systems — prompting, fine-tuning, tool use, and reasoning. That combination is the job: you know when a fine-tuned segmentation model beats a VLM, when a rule engine beats both, and how to compose all three into a system more accurate than any single model. You treat frontier models as components to be measured, pushed, and engineered — never as magic.

Most of all, you're energized by building things that have never existed, and comfortable when the problem, the data, and the definition of success all have to be invented at once.

The Problems You'll Work On

Composite AI systems and credit assignment.
Our most demanding systems chain vision transformers, segmentation models, VLM reasoning, and rule engines. When the pipeline is wrong, which component failed? One of the most interesting open problems in applied ML.

Document understanding beyond the frontier.
Blueprints, site plans, policy stacks, contracts, clinical records — dense, multimodal documents that break off-the-shelf models. You'll build models that actually read them.

Agents that learn from real work.
Our deployments generate verified, ground-truth outcomes on every decision — reward signals most labs can only simulate. You'll help design the data, evals, and training loops to build and fine-tune agents on them.

Evaluation as a product discipline.
When a regulator has to trust your system, evals are the product. You'll build eval suites and failure-mode taxonomies rigorous enough to earn institutional sign-off.

Institutional Intelligence that compounds.
Every verified correction improves the system twice: the corrected fact percolates to every application, and the system that builds the intelligence learns to build it better. You'll work on both loops.

In This Role, You Will

Turn ambiguity into shipped systems
— from no problem statement, no labeled data, and no agreed definition of success, to well-posed ML problems and production deployments.

Own AI systems end-to-end.
There is no handoff: the person who trains the model owns its behavior in production.

Work at the research frontier with production stakes
, applying LLMs, RL fine-tuning, and agentic systems where the output is a decision an institution acts on.

Work directly with the institutions we serve
— permit reviewers, underwriters, compliance officers — to understand how decisions actually get made and ensure your systems change how the work gets done.

Engineer for production reality
, navigating accuracy, latency, cost, and reliability in environments far messier than any benchmark.

Raise the bar across the company
through design reviews, our internal paper club, and the shared playbook for AI systems institutions can trust.

Compensation

We pay competitively for every role and back that with meaningful equity, because we want the people building Brain Co. to genuinely share in what we build together. Beyond salary and equity, we invest in country-specific benefits because we want our team to feel taken care of, not only compensated.

The annual base salary range for this role is $190,000 - $325,000
. We publish this range for every role, as a matter of policy regardless of whether local law requires it. Actual pay will depend on skills, scope, and experience.

new_jobs.description:
Who We Are

Joybuy is JD.com’s dedicated retail platform for Europe, offering products across a wide range of categories. Operating across the UK, Netherlands, Germany, France, Belgium and Luxembourg, we’re building the future of retail through smart systems, bold ideas, and a customer-first mindset. Backed by JD.com, also known as JINGDONG, and its trusted global technology and supply chain ecosystem, we deliver a shopping experience that is speedy, reliable, and genuinely enjoyable. If you’re ready to make a difference, bring your talent and grow with us. Don’t just buy, Joybuy.

Learn more about who we are and what we do: https://about.joybuy.com/about/

What We Offer

Joining Joybuy means becoming part of a business where people, innovation, and impact work together to shape the future of cross-border e-commerce. You’ll contribute to smart supply chains, efficient logistics, and meaningful projects that drive real customer value. With a competitive salary, great office locations, and a supportive, people-first culture, you’ll have the space to grow your career, learn from talented colleagues, and make a genuine impact in a fast-expanding international business.

About The Team

You’ll be joining the Joybuy team, which values collaboration, ownership, and a commitment to delivering high-quality results in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.

We are seeking a data-driven and analytical Payment Operations & Risk Analyst to monitor, optimize, and protect our global payment ecosystem. In this role, you will be the frontline investigator tracking payment performance, mitigating fraud, and identifying areas to improve cost efficiency. You will collaborate closely with Product, Engineering, and Risk teams, translating complex transaction data into actionable improvements that safeguard company funds and enhance customer experience. If you love solving data puzzles, mapping out technical user journeys, and supporting international scaling, this role is for you.

What You Will Do

Order & Payment Scheme Design and Implementation Focus on the full-chain of cross-border e-commerce order transactions; lead the business solution design for platform transaction payments, order settlement, and receivables/collection disbursement. Deeply adapt to cross-border platform trading rules; deliver standardized transaction payment & settlement solutions tailored to different merchants, transaction scenarios and order types, supporting the scaled and standardized expansion of platform order transaction business.
Transaction Payment System Requirements & Development Deeply participate in iterative development and functional optimization of the order transaction payment system; focus on core transaction payment scenarios. Take charge of business-side requirements research, transaction link flow mapping, and payment process design; independently output business solutions and collaborate with product, R&D and risk control teams to deliver core capabilities.
Payment Service & Process Optimization Continuously review and address pain points across the end-to-end order transaction payment chain. Run dedicated optimization initiatives targeting key issues, including transaction payment failures, abnormal order settlement, delayed collection, stuck funds, transaction rejections, and compensation/dispute handling. Iterate on the transaction payment operational processes to drive up the overall order transaction success rate.
Cross-departmental Project Execution Coordinate with business, operations, risk control and technical teams to drive dedicated optimization projects for order transaction payment and settlement. Follow the full lifecycle of requirements review, system development, feature testing, pilot (gray) launch, acceptance and iteration to ensure the payment system capability matches the platform's order transaction business growth rhythm.
Transaction Data Review & Best-practice Accumulation Own monitoring and control of core payment data metrics, including transaction success rate, settlement timeliness, and abnormal transactions ratio. Complete issue attribution and performance review; issue regular transaction payment analysis reports. Accumulate standardized cross-border order transaction payment solutions, risk handling case studies chers, and best practices.

About You

Experience: 2-5 years of experience in payment operations, data analytics, fraud risk management, or a closely related role within fintech or e-commerce.
Payment Knowledge: Solid understanding of the fundamental payment lifecycle, including gateways, acquiring, card schemes, chargebacks, and settlements.
Data Proficiency: Strong analytical skills with hands-on experience querying and visualizing transaction data (using SQL, Excel, Tableau, or Power BI).
Risk Awareness: Familiarity with online fraud detection concepts, chargeback processes, and risk mitigation tools (e.g., 3D Secure, risk scoring).
Cross-Border Exposure: Basic understanding of multi-currency transactions, international payment processing, or alternative payment methods (APMs) is a plus.
Communication & Collaboration: Ability to clearly communicate technical findings to cross-functional teams, including engineering, risk, and product managers.
Detail-Oriented Problem Solver: A proactive mindset with an eye for detail, capable of spotting a subtle trend shift in large datasets before it becomes a widespread issue.

new_jobs.title: RCSA & Internal Control Analyst
new_jobs.description:
SATS Ltd

Who We Are

Headquartered in Singapore, SATS Ltd. is one of the world’s largest providers of air cargo handling services and Asia’s leading airline caterer. SATS Gateway Services provides airfreight and ground handling services including passenger services, ramp and baggage handling, aviation security services, aircraft cleaning and aviation laundry. SATS Food Solutions serves airlines, institutions, and operates central kitchens with large-scale food production and distribution capabilities for a wide range of cuisines. SATS is present in the Asia-Pacific, the Americas, Europe, the Middle East and Africa, powering an interconnected world of trade, travel and taste. Following the acquisition of Worldwide Flight Services (WFS) in 2023, the combined SATS and WFS network operates over 215 stations in 27 countries. These cover trade routes responsible for more than 50% of global air cargo volume. SATS has been listed on the Singapore Exchange since May 2000. For more information, please visit www.sats.com.sg

The Role

To support the rollout and ongoing maintenance of the EMEA RCSA framework and related internal control activities, we are looking for an RCSA & Internal Control Analyst to join the team. Working alongside the EMEA Risk & Control Manager, the successful candidate will provide day-to-day operational support, including coordination, follow-up, documentation and data consolidation. This will help accelerate the rollout, improve consistency across countries and establish a sustainable long-term operating model, while allowing the EMEA Risk & Control Manager to remain focused on governance, stakeholder management and overall framework oversight.

The role will support the rollout, documentation, testing and maintenance of country-level Risk and Control Self-Assessments (RCSA) and related internal control activities across EMEA. It will help ensure that risk and control information is accurately collected, structured, tracked and kept up to date in coordination with local stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities

Support the implementation and ongoing development of the EMEA Risk and Control Self-Assessment (RCSA) framework, working with country teams to identify, assess and manage risks in line with the Group's risk management methodology.
Work collaboratively with stakeholders across a range of business functions, including Operations, Finance, Legal and Health, Safety, Security and Environment (HSSE), to understand local processes, identify potential risks and establish appropriate controls.
Support the identification and assessment of country-specific risks, documenting existing controls, potential gaps and compensating controls to help ensure risks are appropriately managed.
Develop and maintain local risk and control registers, ensuring information is accurate, up to date and aligned with regional requirements.
Work with local stakeholders to harmonise risk management approaches and control frameworks across EMEA, promoting consistency while taking account of country-specific requirements and differences in local maturity.
Support the implementation of the RCSA framework across EMEA countries, coordinating activities, gathering and consolidating information, monitoring progress and following up with stakeholders to ensure timely completion.
Support second-line (Line 2) control testing activities, including coordinating evidence collection, reviewing supporting documentation and following up on outstanding information or identified control gaps.
Contribute to compliance activities, including the ongoing monitoring and documentation of anti-corruption and accounting controls in support of Sapin II requirements.
Track action plans, remediation activities and outstanding issues, working with local stakeholders to monitor progress, address delays and ensure agreed actions are completed.
Build effective working relationships across countries and functions, encouraging collaboration, knowledge-sharing and consistent approaches to risk management in an international, matrixed organisation.
Identify opportunities to improve risk and control processes, documentation and procedures, contributing to the continuous development of a consistent and sustainable EMEA control framework.

Educational Qualifications

A degree or equivalent professional experience in Risk Management, Business, Finance, Compliance or a related discipline would be advantageous.
Ongoing commitment to training and professional development in risk, compliance and audit processes.

Relevant Skills And Experience

2–5 years' experience in risk management, internal controls, compliance or a related field.
Experience working with risk and compliance frameworks, including risk identification, assessment and control implementation.
Experience working in an international business or matrix organisation, engaging stakeholders across multiple countries and functions.
Good understanding of operational processes and internal controls across different business functions.
Strong organisational, analytical and communication skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and build effective working relationships.
Confident managing documentation, risk registers, trackers and supporting evidence, with strong attention to detail.
Able to work autonomously, take ownership of tasks and manage competing deadlines.

Personal Characteristics & Behaviours

Resilient and adaptable: Comfortable navigating challenges, working through ambiguity and maintaining momentum when faced with competing priorities or differing levels of risk maturity across countries.
Curious and analytical: Naturally inquisitive, with the confidence to ask questions, challenge assumptions and develop an understanding of risks across different business functions.
A relationship builder: Able to establish trust, communicate effectively and work collaboratively with stakeholders at different levels and across different countries.
Structured in approach: Able to bring order to complex or ambiguous situations, organise information clearly and establish consistent ways of working.
Reliable and accountable: Takes ownership of responsibilities and works closely with the EMEA Risk & Control Manager to support decision-making.

Travel Requirements

Travel within country/region/international may be required on ad hoc or regular basis

Core Values

We have 5 core People Values at SATS.

Safety: Safety – its ingrained in our DNA

Customer Focus: Every smile is a win for us

Respect: We strive to listen, understand and respect.

Excellence: Excellence isn’t just a goal, it’s the SATS way.

Teamwork: We don’t just collaborate. We amplify each other’s strengths.

These reveal fresh insights for our clients; helping them to build better products and brands, to deliver effective marketing to consumers.

Natural Language Processing, GPT & other LLMs
: unearthing trends, themes and other patterns from large text-based data sets, and deploying state-of-the-art AI to automate and empower consumer facing businesses and their insights & analytics functions
Marketing Data Science & Personalisation

Data Engineering & Data Architecture
: data engineering across a variety of tools to integrate these leading technologies into optimised and efficient data models and ecosystems, feeding into best-in-class analytics dashboards, marketing activation and front-end platforms

full stack expertise to build, maintain and support internal and externally facing Software & Data as a Service solutions, in AWS, that accelerate delivery and unlock deeper insights for our clients

As a start-up, we can move faster than most companies and do things differently. We have experienced rapid growth so far and we’re looking for a Data Engineer to join our growing team.

You’ll play a crucial role in designing, building and productionising innovative data pipelines, in the cloud, from scratch. Experience with designing efficient physical data models/schemas and developing ETL/ELT scripts

Experience developing data solutions in cloud environments such as Azure, AWS or GCP – Azure Databricks & Snowflake experience a bonus

new_jobs.title: Data Scientist
new_jobs.description:
Fospha is the measurement system enterprise retail and ecommerce brands run their business on. We give marketing teams one clear, daily view of what's actually working — across every channel and everywhere they sell, from their website to Amazon and TikTok Shop — down to the level of a single ad or piece of creative. It replaces guesswork and gut feel with a number marketing, finance and agencies can all trust and act on.

Brands including Dyson, Gymshark, Adanola and Huel use Fospha up to 25 times a day to decide where budget should move next. We've spent over a decade building this, with more than $40 billion in marketing spend now optimised through the platform — and we're scaling fast across London, Mumbai and Austin.

About The Role

We're looking for a Data Scientist
to join Fospha's Data Science team in London.

Fospha builds marketing measurement products for ecommerce brands — attribution, marketing mix modelling, incrementality testing, and brand impact measurement. Our Data Science team owns the models behind all of it, from methodology through to production code. You will work across our technical stacks and own maintaining and growing the codebases that power our product and solutions.

This role suits an established data scientist who wants to own things properly. You'll lead larger production projects, choose the modelling approach rather than being handed it, and talk to clients as the modelling expert in the room — supported by a team that reviews each other's work seriously, and a company that rewards high agency with ownership.

Team:
Data Science

Level:
Career (Data Science Career Development Framework)

Location:
London

What you'll do

Lead larger production projects end to end — scoping, building, and shipping production-level code, rather than working through tickets someone else has specified
Choose the modelling approach — independently selecting and applying the right method within our suite, across attribution, marketing mix modelling, incrementality testing, and brand impact. You will be given time to keep up-to-date on the latest methodologies in the industry
Resolve bugs and queries independently — including in parts of the codebase you didn't write, without needing to route them upwards
Use AI as leverage, not as a crutch — solving coding tickets quickly, unblocking yourself on product and engineering dependencies, and building automation workflows that save the team time
Work with QA properly — using our automated tooling efficiently and flagging the gaps in it rather than working around them
Communicate as a modelling expert — confidently and independently, with clients and with colleagues, including when the message is that a number they like is wrong
Help develop the people around you — code review, methodology critique, and hands-on support for less experienced colleagues. Breaking down tickets and helping those more junior is essential

What we're looking for

Essential

Solid commercial data science experience — typically 3–5 years, with a track record of shipping models into production
Strong ML knowledge across multiple algorithm families, and the judgement to pick the right approach for the problem rather than the one you know best
Strong Python and SQL, with the ability to lead on production-level code and set the standard others work to
Able to debug and resolve issues independently across unfamiliar repositories, using AI tooling to accelerate rather than to guess, while still understanding the problem fully
Strong AI fluency — you solve tickets quickly with it, you unblock cross-department dependencies with it, you build automation workflows with it, and you never send AI-assisted output without checking it
Confident, independent communication with clients and stakeholders as the technical authority on the work
Emerging mentorship — you're ready to develop junior colleagues, and you want to
Initiative in accepting and planning your own work, rather than waiting to be allocated it
Genuine attention to detail — much of this work involves noticing when a number is wrong

Nice to have

Bayesian modelling experience, particularly hierarchical models
Experience with AWS or comparable cloud tooling
Familiarity with automated QA tooling and test coverage practices
Experience with marketing, ecommerce, or advertising data

Not required

Experience with attribution methodology, MMM, incrementality testing, or Bayesian modelling is genuinely an advantage at this level — but it isn't a filter. Our stack takes time to learn regardless of what you arrive with, and we'd rather hire strong modelling judgement and teach the domain.

How You'll Grow

We run a published Data Science Career Development Framework with six levels. You'd join at Career, where the expectations are:

AI Fluency & Tooling:
Leverages AI to solve coding tickets quickly; consistently unblocks themselves on cross-department dependencies, especially product and engineering; never sends AI-assisted communication without checking quality; expert at using AI to build automation workflows.

Machine Learning & Modelling:
Strong ML knowledge across multiple algorithm families; independently chooses and applies the right modelling approach within Fospha's suite.

Engineering & Codebase:
Leads on larger coding projects and tickets with production-level code; resolves queries and bugs efficiently and independently; master at using supplied AWS tooling through AI; uses automated QA tools efficiently and flags gaps to the QA team.

Stakeholder & Communication:
Confidently and independently communicates with clients and colleagues as a modelling expert; assists with the development of junior members of staff.

Job Complexity:
Consistent contributor and respected knowledge holder, with emerging collaboration and mentorship abilities.

Supervision:
Demonstrates initiative in accepting and planning work.

Progression to Advanced
level is against explicit, published criteria — taking on almost any ticket efficiently, building and planning production repositories, collaborating with product on project outcomes and estimates, actively developing junior colleagues, and representing Fospha as a trusted external voice on modelling in senior client and partner conversations. You'll know what you're working towards from your first week.

Throughout, we look for the same core behaviours: concise communication, collaboration, problem solving, critical thinking, growth mindset, attention to detail, time management, and initiative.

Why Fospha

Real methodological depth. Bayesian attribution, MMM, geo lift testing, and causal inference are our day job, not a side project. You'll be working on all of it, not adjacent to it.
Ownership at the methodology level. At this level you're choosing the approach, not implementing someone else's choice.
Published career framework. No guessing what the next level requires or when you'll get there.
A team that reviews each other's work properly. Code review and methodology critique from people who care about getting the model right.
Direct client impact. The models you build and maintain drive real budget decisions at brands you'll recognise.

The University of Sheffield is a remarkable place to work. Our people are at the heart of everything we do. Their diverse backgrounds, abilities and beliefs make Sheffield a world-class university.

We offer a fantastic range of benefits including a highly competitive annual leave entitlement (with the ability to purchase more), a generous pensions scheme, flexible working opportunities, a commitment to your development and wellbeing, a wide range of retail discounts, and much more. Overview

Are you a passionate researcher eager to bridge the gap between advanced engineering and clinical practice to tackle a transformative healthcare challenge? We have an exciting opportunity in the School of Mechanical, Aerospace and Civil Engineering for a Research Associate to apply their skills in biomedical engineering to revolutionize haemodialysis and make a profound impact on global health.

You will join the Thermofluids Group at the University of Sheffield, working in close collaboration with experts in the School of Medicine and Population Health and Sheffield Teaching Hospitals. As a key member of this interdisciplinary project, you will lead the design, assembly, and clinical validation of a novel dialyser prototype.

You will be responsible for testing the prototype using blood-mimicking fluids and, ultimately, human blood to assess cleaning efficiency, clotting risk, and biocompatibility.

This role offers a unique opportunity to apply fundamental engineering principles to real-world physiological conditions. You will work in close collaboration with two other Research Associates focusing on numerical simulations and experimental fluid dynamics, contributing directly to a greener, more efficient future for nephrology.

Main Duties And Responsibilities

Lead the assembly of the prototype, ensuring tight tolerances for spinning components, robust sealing, and integration of semi-permeable membranes. You will troubleshoot technical issues during assembly to ensure the prototype is ready for testing.
Conduct rigorous solute removal efficiency tests using Human Peripheral Simulated Blood Plasma (BZ464). You will measure the clearance rates of key metabolites, including urea, creatinine, and phosphate, to optimize the operational parameters of the dialyser.
Manage the ethical procurement and testing of voluntarily donated human blood to assess biocompatibility. You will evaluate the prototype for fibrin strands, check transmembrane pressure, and analyse blood samples for clotting and haemolysis markers, ensuring safety standards are met.
Work closely with the fluids engineering PDRAs to translate simulation and experimental results into physiological insights. You will actively participate in weekly meetings with renal clinicians at Sheffield Teaching Hospitals to interpret data and refine the device design based on clinical feedback.
Maintain meticulous records of experimental methodologies and results in compliance with clinical governance frameworks. You will contribute to the writing of high-impact journal publications, present outcomes at international medical and engineering conferences, and participate in public engagement events regarding sustainable nephrology.
Carry out other duties, commensurate with the grade and remit of the post.

new_jobs.description:
The University of Sheffield is a remarkable place to work. Our people are at the heart of everything we do. Their diverse backgrounds, abilities and beliefs make Sheffield a world-class university.

We offer a fantastic range of benefits including a highly competitive annual leave entitlement (with the ability to purchase more), a generous pensions scheme, flexible working opportunities, a commitment to your development and wellbeing, a wide range of retail discounts, and much more. Find out more about our benefits (opens in a new window) and join us to become part of something special.

The School of Mathematical and Physical Sciences is seeking to appoint a Research Associate in Theoretical Cosmology. This post is funded by the Royal Society through Dr Eleonora Di Valentino’s Dorothy Hodgkin Fellowship renewal for the project “H0 Tension Test” (H0TTEST) and is fixed term for 12 months.

The project investigates whether tensions in cosmological observations, particularly the Hubble constant tension, arise from unaccounted-for systematic effects or indicate new physics beyond the standard ΛCDM model. It combines theoretical modelling, cosmological data analysis and numerical methods to explore extensions involving dark energy, dark matter, neutrino physics, inflation and modified gravity. You will contribute to testing cosmological models with current observations and assessing their predictions for forthcoming surveys, with scope to develop research directions that reflect your expertise and interests within the project’s aims.

You will work with Dr Eleonora Di Valentino within the Cosmology, Relativity and Gravitation group, which comprises five academic staff (Dr Eleonora Di Valentino, Dr Sam Dolan, Dr Steffen Gielen, Professor Carsten van de Bruck and Professor Elizabeth Winstanley) and six PhD students. The group’s expertise spans cosmology, gravitation and mathematical physics, with an active seminar programme and close links to colleagues in statistics and astrophysics, providing a stimulating environment to develop your research career. Funds will be available to support professional development, including participation in conferences, collaboration meetings and research visits.

You should have a PhD in physics, astronomy, cosmology or a closely related discipline, or equivalent experience. We welcome candidates with a strong research background in cosmology and expertise in one or more of the following: cosmological data analysis, statistical inference, theoretical modelling or numerical simulations. We are looking for evidence of research achievement and potential, strong computational and analytical skills, and the ability to develop independent ideas and work collaboratively.

Main Duties And Responsibilities

Contribute to and support the work of the research group (e.g. by giving and attending local working seminars and participating in collaborations).
Prepare high-quality research publications.
Prepare papers for journals / presentations either in-house or at national/international conferences to disseminate research findings.
Attend international conferences, and give talks on the work of the research group.
Read academic papers, journals and text books to keep abreast of developments and use this information to brief colleagues and inform the work of the project.
This is not a teaching role, however teaching experience may be available if the successful candidate is interested in gaining some teaching experience. This will be dependent upon opportunities being available within the department.
As a member of staff you will be encouraged to make ethical decisions in your role, embedding the University sustainability strategy into your working activities wherever possible.
Carry out other duties, commensurate with the grade and remit of the post

Our diverse community of staff and students recognises the unique abilities, backgrounds, and beliefs of all. We foster a culture where everyone feels they belong and are respected. Role – Incident Response Analyst (Cyber Security)

Rate – upto £450/Day Outside IR35

12 Months contract
